scope: Follow-up of the 200 incomplete profile claims

reviews.claimText: Stay on open trails. Use binoculars and avoid flash or shining a light into its eyes.
reviews.note: Trail and lighting advice matches NParks guidance; handling cautions follow the professional-help guidance.

reviews.claimText: Never touch or attempt to rescue one by hand. Do not use flash photography or lure it into view.
reviews.note: Trail and lighting advice matches NParks guidance; handling cautions follow the professional-help guidance.

reviews.claimText: Do not pursue it or disclose a den location. Report suspected trapping to the relevant wildlife authority.
reviews.note: Sections 1–3 and 5 support these distance, disturbance and reporting precautions.

reviews.claimText: Enjoy it from the path. Do not bait it for a photograph or offer snacks.
reviews.note: Sections 1–3 and 5 support these distance, disturbance and reporting precautions.

reviews.claimText: Remain on trails and let it disappear into cover. Do not pursue it for a closer photograph.
reviews.note: Sections 1–3 and 5 support these distance, disturbance and reporting precautions.

reviews.claimText: Keep to permitted paths, observe quietly and never feed or pursue it. Leave dense undergrowth undisturbed and do not share exact resting locations.
reviews.note: Sections 1–3 and 5 support these distance, disturbance and reporting precautions.

reviews.claimText: Keep a generous distance and never block its path or approach a burrow. Do not attempt to handle an animal or remove its quills.
reviews.note: Sections 1–3 and 5 support these distance, disturbance and reporting precautions.

reviews.claimText: Use binoculars from permitted paths and leave resting animals undisturbed. Never bait, feed, touch or follow a civet into the forest.
reviews.note: Sections 1–3 and 5 support these distance, disturbance and reporting precautions.

reviews.claimText: Observe from permitted routes and avoid flash, sustained spotlighting or disturbance of tree holes. Never lure an animal with food or enter closed areas to seek it.
reviews.note: NParks lighting guidance supplements the linked photography and wildlife precautions.

reviews.claimText: Watch quietly from open trails without flash or prolonged direct light. Do not inspect occupied tree cavities or publish exact shelter locations.
reviews.note: NParks lighting guidance supplements the linked photography and wildlife precautions.

reviews.claimText: Keep to open paths, leave it where it is and avoid handling or flash. Do not disclose a precise location or collect an animal for a pet.
reviews.note: NParks lighting guidance supplements the linked photography and wildlife precautions.

reviews.claimText: Use open trails and binoculars. Do not follow a group off-trail, play calls or share sensitive locations.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Listen quietly from paths. Never play calls to draw it out, set up bait or publicise a nest.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Leave fruit for wildlife. Do not feed, crowd or approach a nesting cavity.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Use binoculars from a safe viewpoint. Never fly a drone near a nest or move closer to force a take-off.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Listen from a distance and avoid playback. Do not search for or interfere with a host nest.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Watch feeding birds from the path. Avoid pointing out or approaching active nests.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Use binoculars from a fixed point. Let the bird resume hunting rather than following it between perches.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Do not feed or chase. Give hens with chicks room to move and leave ground nests alone.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Watch from open paths using binoculars. Avoid flash, prolonged torchlight, playback or crowding a resting bird. Never approach a nest or publish its precise position.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Remain on public paths and give bank vegetation space. Do not clear branches for photographs, bait the bird, play calls or approach a burrow entrance.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Use coastal hides and public paths. Stay off restricted islands and mangrove nesting areas. Give a feeding bird space instead of following it along the waterline.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Scan the canopy from public trails. Never bait a raptor or approach an occupied nest. Keep the bird's flight path clear and watch through binoculars.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Use hides and stay on public paths. Do not enter reedbeds, cut vegetation or flush a hidden bird into view. Keep nesting habitat undisturbed.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Stay on paths and use binoculars. Do not enter colonies, feed birds or approach nests for photographs.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Watch from paths or hides. Avoid making birds fly away from feeding or resting areas, and never feed them.
reviews.note: The linked guidance supports these conservative viewing precautions. It is advice, not measured species behaviour.

reviews.claimText: Listen after rain from a safe path. Leave adults, eggs and tadpoles in place.
reviews.note: Trail, water and wildlife guidance supports leaving animals and their habitat undisturbed; playback avoidance is conservative advice.

reviews.claimText: Do not peel open foam nests, collect tadpoles or handle the frogs. Watch from the path.
reviews.note: Trail, water and wildlife guidance supports leaving animals and their habitat undisturbed; playback avoidance is conservative advice.

reviews.claimText: Stay out of streams and leave turtles, eggs and cover undisturbed. Do not collect or release pet turtles into natural habitats.
reviews.note: Trail, water and wildlife guidance supports leaving animals and their habitat undisturbed; playback avoidance is conservative advice.

reviews.claimText: Listen from open trails during permitted hours. Do not use call playback, move leaf litter, enter breeding streams or handle frogs and eggs.
reviews.note: Trail, water and wildlife guidance supports leaving animals and their habitat undisturbed; playback avoidance is conservative advice.

reviews.claimText: Observe without moving logs or leaves. Keep out of streams, avoid playback and flash, and leave amphibians and tadpoles untouched.
reviews.note: Trail, water and wildlife guidance supports leaving animals and their habitat undisturbed; playback avoidance is conservative advice.

reviews.claimText: Usually has one baby at a time. Young may ride on the mother’s tail or back while she moves.
reviews.note: Habitat and ecology confirms one baby, carried on the mother's back or tail.

reviews.claimText: Least Concern · 2008
reviews.note: The published study explicitly cites Boeadi and Steinmetz (2008) for Least Concern. This verifies the dated category.

reviews.claimText: Critically Endangered · 2019
reviews.note: The paper explicitly links Critically Endangered to Challender et al. (2019), the dated IUCN assessment.

reviews.claimText: Vulnerable · 2021
reviews.note: Wildlife Institute of India gives Vulnerable and cites the 2021 IUCN assessment for this taxon.

reviews.claimText: Road crossings, disturbance and unsafe encounters can affect urban families. Connected, usable waterways remain important.
reviews.note: The Singapore mortality study documents vehicle collisions; AVS covers disturbance. Waterway connectivity is a conservation inference.

reviews.claimText: A rare forest resident recorded in the nature reserves and Pulau Tekong. This guide withholds precise observation and resting locations.
reviews.note: Distribution lists both central reserves and Pulau Tekong. Exact sites remain withheld as an editorial precaution.

reviews.claimText: Endangered · 2020
reviews.note: The conservation section explicitly cites IUCN 2020 for Endangered under Nycticebus coucang.

reviews.claimText: Critically Endangered · 2022
reviews.note: IUCN's Asian langur report lists Presbytis femoralis as Critically Endangered, assessed in 2022.

reviews.claimText: Critically Endangered · 2018
reviews.note: NParks explicitly identifies the August 2018 global assessment as Critically Endangered.

reviews.claimText: Forages in thick foliage near water and forest edges. Its loud, bubbling song is a useful clue, but listening must not become playback or disturbance.
reviews.note: The species ecology account supports foliage, waterside foraging and song; birdwatching guidance supports avoiding playback.

reviews.claimText: An egg-laying bird whose nesting cover needs protection. Do not seek nests or publish nest locations; local timing is not predicted by this guide.
reviews.note: NParks records a nest and eggs. Its birdwatching guidance supports the nesting precautions; no local calendar is inferred.

reviews.claimText: Mainly fruit, supplemented by small animals.
reviews.note: The field account records fruit and animal food, with undamaged seed regurgitation. Dispersal is qualitative, not a local rate.

reviews.claimText: Fruit consumption can move seeds between patches of vegetation.
reviews.note: The field account records fruit and animal food, with undamaged seed regurgitation. Dispersal is qualitative, not a local rate.

reviews.claimText: Critically Endangered · 2008
reviews.note: IUCN's marine-status chapter records approval of Critically Endangered in May 2008 for this species.

reviews.claimText: Least Concern · 2025
reviews.note: IUCN's 10 October 2025 announcement explicitly records the global change to Least Concern. Local status remains separate.

reviews.claimText: Endangered · 2025
reviews.note: IUCN confirms that the reassessment retained Endangered in the 2025-2 update after petition review.

reviews.claimText: Mainly diurnal.
reviews.note: AVS describes daytime foraging, forest-edge encounters, feeding effects and the stated encounter precautions.

reviews.claimText: Commonly encountered in and around forest reserves and some parkland. Feeding changes natural foraging behaviour and increases conflict.
reviews.note: AVS describes daytime foraging, forest-edge encounters, feeding effects and the stated encounter precautions.

reviews.claimText: Keep food out of sight, secure bags and give the group space. Do not stare, feed, tease or try to touch a monkey.
reviews.note: AVS describes daytime foraging, forest-edge encounters, feeding effects and the stated encounter precautions.

reviews.claimText: Roots through the ground for food. Females may travel with young; an animal with piglets or no escape route needs particular space.
reviews.note: AVS covers soil digging, protective mothers, road conflict, feeding effects and distance from piglets.

reviews.claimText: An omnivore whose rooting changes soil and leaf litter.
reviews.note: AVS covers soil digging, protective mothers, road conflict, feeding effects and distance from piglets.

reviews.claimText: Human food, roads and encounters near urban edges can lead to conflict. Never encourage it to approach people.
reviews.note: AVS covers soil digging, protective mothers, road conflict, feeding effects and distance from piglets.

reviews.claimText: Stay calm, keep your distance and avoid separating adults from piglets. Do not feed or corner a boar.
reviews.note: AVS covers soil digging, protective mothers, road conflict, feeding effects and distance from piglets.

reviews.claimText: Widespread and commonly seen near people. Its national assessment is Not Applicable because it is introduced.
reviews.note: AVS confirms introduced, abundant urban occurrence; the NParks national table assigns Not Applicable.

reviews.claimText: Common in secondary woodland, gardens, parks and other urban greenery. It is a native resident, not an introduced noise-making species.
reviews.note: AVS records secondary forest, parks and urban habitat; the national table confirms native origin.

reviews.claimText: Loss of fruiting trees removes food. Managing noise complaints should not involve disturbing wildlife nests.
reviews.note: Fruit dependence supports the food-tree inference. NParks nesting guidance supports avoiding nest disturbance during noise complaints.

reviews.claimText: Least Concern · 2016
reviews.note: The research paper explicitly cites BirdLife International (2016) for this taxon's Least Concern status.

reviews.claimText: Widespread in parks, gardens and other wooded settings. It is listed as native and nationally Least Concern.
reviews.note: The ecology account confirms parks, gardens and wooded sites; the national table confirms native origin and Least Concern.

reviews.claimText: Blue-green upperparts with a white collar and belly. The large bill is dark, unlike the red bill of a white-throated kingfisher.
reviews.note: The species account confirms blue upperparts, white collar and black bill; the comparative article covers the white-throated species.

reviews.claimText: Usually produces one well-developed young. Regional accounts describe a pregnancy of roughly five months; this is not a prediction of Singapore birth dates. Juveniles were documented during the Ubin rediscovery study.
reviews.note: ADW supports one precocial young and roughly five months' gestation; the Ubin study independently records a juvenile.

reviews.claimText: Rediscovered on an offshore island in 2005. Later camera-trap records documented animals in mainland forest reserves and other wooded areas. RDB3 continues to recognise a native, nationally Critically Endangered population.
reviews.note: The 2016 paper documents offshore rediscovery in 2005 and later mainland records. RDB3 confirms native, nationally Critically Endangered.

reviews.claimText: Recorded in Singapore's central forest reserves and in a wooded nature park outside them. Local records require careful identification; difficulty seeing a nocturnal animal is not a population estimate.
reviews.note: Chua et al. (2013) documents the additional localities, alongside earlier central-reserve records. Survey detections are not population estimates.

reviews.claimText: Recorded from Bukit Timah and Central Catchment forests. The latter records were published in 2013, so the older statement that it occurs only in Bukit Timah is not retained.
reviews.note: Chua et al. (2013) documents the additional localities, alongside earlier central-reserve records. Survey detections are not population estimates.

reviews.claimText: A documented Singapore nesting observation found a chick in a bird's-nest fern in 2016. Such records establish local breeding, but do not provide a complete island-wide breeding calendar.
reviews.note: The April 2016 direct observation documents a chick in a bird's-nest fern, not an island-wide breeding season.

reviews.claimText: Bird Society of Singapore lists it as an uncommon resident that favours dense woodland and mangroves. NParks has also documented use of the Eco-Link@BKE wildlife bridge; the bridge is not a public viewing site.
reviews.note: The bird account supports resident habitat. NParks confirms bridge use and research-only access.

reviews.claimText: A common native frog of suburban and rural greenery, as well as disturbed forest. It is nationally Least Concern in RDB3.
reviews.note: The ecology account supports human habitation and forest-edge occurrence; RDB3 confirms native origin and Least Concern.

reviews.claimText: Grey and white plumage, long legs, a long neck and a yellowish pointed bill. Adults have a dark stripe extending behind the eye.
reviews.note: ADW's physical, feeding and behaviour sections support this field. Food-web transfer is a qualitative inference.

reviews.claimText: Fish and other small animals captured near water.
reviews.note: ADW's physical, feeding and behaviour sections support this field. Food-web transfer is a qualitative inference.

reviews.claimText: Can feed during daylight or at night, depending on conditions.
reviews.note: ADW's physical, feeding and behaviour sections support this field. Food-web transfer is a qualitative inference.

reviews.claimText: Often waits motionless before striking at prey. It usually draws its neck back during flight.
reviews.note: ADW's physical, feeding and behaviour sections support this field. Food-web transfer is a qualitative inference.

reviews.claimText: Transfers energy from aquatic prey into the wider wetland food web.
reviews.note: ADW's physical, feeding and behaviour sections support this field. Food-web transfer is a qualitative inference.
